label: Total Crossings (Jul 30 - Aug 4)
source: House of Commons Library / CNN / Ceuta city government
contestNote: Spanish Interior Ministry initially said 49,000-50,000 in 24 hours; Mayor Vivas said 60,000; cumulative full-crisis estimates range up to 80,000.

label: Confirmed Deaths
contestNote: Rose from an initial 72 (Aug 2) to 86 (Sky News) to 111 (100 in Ceuta, 11 in Fnideq) by Aug 4; some later-recovered bodies not definitively linked to the crisis. NGO Caminando Fronteras separately tallies 141 (Aug 5), a figure Spanish officials confirmed to media without formally adopting as the state count. A one-month retrospective by The Olive Press (Aug 30) cites 'more than 150' deaths, the highest figure yet reported, though without a new recovery operation or itemised count to explain the increase over the NGO tally.

label: Migrants Still in Ceuta
contestNote: Spain's government puts the figure at roughly 5,000 as of Aug 30 (1,827 already housed at the Loma Margarita and El Embolsamiento centres, out of ~72,000 who entered irregularly in late July); Ceuta city and other estimates range 6,500-9,000. Ceuta's Assembly unanimously declared the city in an 'extreme situation, on the verge of collapse' on Aug 28, and Madrid asked Frontex, Europol and the EUAA to reinforce migrant triage. On Aug 30, Secretary of State for Security Aina Calvo relocated to Ceuta to directly oversee the operation, with a two-week target to move remaining migrants off the streets.

label: Beach Camp Migrants Relocated to Shelters
contestNote: Transferred to two new temporary reception centres, Loma Margarita and El Embolsamiento (1,800 combined initial capacity), as police cleared the El Trampolín beach camp. About 500 people returned to the beach hours later, forcing a second eviction attempt Aug 21; Ceuta city government warned it would suspend beach-cleaning operations if migrants kept returning. Migration Minister Elma Saiz says capacity could expand to ~4,000 places via four additional sites.

label: Unaccompanied Minors Identified
contestNote: Revised up from the ~1,500 reported Aug 26 (which followed a database de-duplication audit). The Sept 1 figure of 2,678 comes from the Ministry of Childhood and comprises 1,478 already registered plus an estimated 1,200 still on the street — a broader count than the earlier 'identified' figure, not a reversal of the de-duplication. At the current transfer rate (~60/month, 720 relocated so far), full relocation via ordinary procedure would take nearly four years; Ceuta has shelter capacity for only 29 minors.

label: CETI Reception Centre Occupancy
contestNote: Unaccompanied-minors facility separately reported at 2,400% of ordinary capacity per Mayor Vivas.

label: EU States Imposing Border Checks on Spain
contestNote: Italy, France, Finland, Austria, Sweden, Denmark and Czechia had each reimposed or announced border controls linked to the crisis.

label: Italy-Spain Schengen Suspension Runs Until
contestNote: Both sides extended a second time on Aug 31: Italy's Interior Ministry notified the EU it is prolonging checks on Spanish arrivals another 15 days (from the original Sep 1 expiry) to roughly Sep 15, citing 5,000-10,000 irregular migrants still in Ceuta; Spain reciprocated, extending its checks on Italian arrivals (previously to Sep 7) a further 15 days to Sep 16. Madrid calls the Italian measure an 'unjustified affront'; Rome says the situation 'is anything but improved.'

label: Hate Speech Posts Logged (Jul 30-31 crossing window)
contestNote: Logged over the two days of the mass crossing alone; part of a broader jump to 57,406 hate-content items in July, up from 40,800 in June. 48% of posts link migration to crime and 40% dehumanise targeted groups.

label: New Urgent Reception Places Approved
contestNote: Capacity more than doubled from 1,800 to over 3,400 places within a week (as of Sept 1), per government officials, who ruled out mainland transfer as the primary response; 6,000-bed target unchanged.

label: Ceuta Business Losses (as of Aug 11)
contestNote: Includes an estimated €10.2M from the cancelled patron-saint festivities alone, plus ~90% August tourism booking cancellations.

label: New Emergency Economic Package for Ceuta
source: Spanish Council of Ministers via Euronews (Aug 30)
contestNote: Sept 1 decree-law: €118M humanitarian/minors' care, €90M security, €80M economic activity support, €21M essential services, plus €50M in loan guarantees, for the remainder of 2026. Supersedes the €165M figure announced Aug 30 (€80M near-term Ceuta economy injection + €70M for 2027), which government officials describe as folded into this broader package rather than additive to it.

label: EU Emergency Migration Funds Requested by Spain
source: Spanish government via Euronews / Libertad Digital (Aug 24)
contestNote: Requested from the EU's FAMI (Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund) and IGFV (Borders and Visa Instrument) to help cover Ceuta's reception, triage and border-management costs.
